alt.title: MG90S Servo, Metal Gear (180 deg)

name: INA219 I2C current sensor, 0.1 ohm shunt

amazon.title: GY-219 INA219 bi-directional DC current sensor breakout (1 set)
amazon.notes: 0.1 ohm 1% shunt, 26 V, +/-3.2 A. Check the board size: this generic layout is about 25.6 x 20.5 mm and fits only beside a Mini560 no longer than 26 mm.

alt.title: INA219 High Side DC Current Sensor Breakout STEMMA QT
alt.notes: Genuine, 0.1 ohm shunt, 20.3 x 22.9 mm: fits beside full-size Mini560s.

alt2.title: INA219 Current Sensor Module (Raspberry Pi Pico)
alt2.notes: Raspberry Pi Pico-format board; costs more than Adafruit's.

build_note: Sits in the servo 5 V line with a second 0.1 ohm resistor across its shunt. Boards up to 23 mm wide fit the power board as drawn; a 25.6 mm clone needs the shorter Mini560.

name: Mini560 fixed 5 V 5 A buck

amazon.title: MECCANIXITY MINI560 7-20V to 5V 5A, 5 pcs
amazon.notes: Fixed 5 V out, 7-20 V in. Many Mini560 listings are 3.3, 9 or 12 V, or adjustable; check the 5V marking. Expect it to need cooling above about 4 A.

alt.title: 5V, 5A Step-Down Voltage Regulator D24V50F5 (item #2851)
alt.notes: The trustworthy option, at about ten times the price of a Mini560. Cheap fixed 5 V Mini560s are easiest to find on eBay and AliExpress.

build_note: Must be the FIXED 5 V version, about 29 x 18 mm. Check the output with a meter before connecting anything.

name: 2S 7.4V LiPo 450 mAh + charger (2-pack)

amazon.title: URGENEX 7.4V 2S 30C 450mAh LiPo, JST & PH2.0, with 1-to-2 USB charger
amazon.notes: Two 450 mAh packs plus a 1-to-2 USB charger, JST and PH2.0 plugs. Packs about 46 x 25 x 9.7 mm, 23-25 g. Replace the plug with a female XT30. Avoid B0H7R5R7HS from the same brand: no charger.
amazon.price_source: typical price for a 2-pack with charger

alt.vendor: AMain Hobbies (battery) + AMain HPI charger + Adafruit pigtail
alt.title: Tattu 2S 75C 450 mAh LiPo (JST) + HPI 2S USB balance charger + JST PH 2-pin female pigtail
alt.notes: Tattu 2S 75C 450 mAh ($7.79, 44 x 25 x 14 mm, 29 g, XH balance lead; thicker than the 12.5 mm limit) + HPI 2S USB balance charger ($11.99, https://www.amainhobbies.com/hpi-2s-7.4v-usb-lipo-balance-dc-charger-hpi160839/p1589267) + Adafruit JST-PH 2-pin pigtail ($0.75, https://www.adafruit.com/product/261). 'JST' on hobby packs usually means RCY/SYP, not PH2.0; if you fit XT30 you do not need the pigtail. Also: ManiaX 2S 30C 450 mAh, $8.99, 62 x 30 x 11 mm, 31 g (https://www.amainhobbies.com/maniax-2s-30c-lipo-battery-pack-7.4v-450mah-w-jst-connector-mx-450-2s-30/p1419597). Stock comes and goes.

build_note: The one expensive component. Pack no thicker than 12.5 mm. Best is a pack sold with an XT30 plug. If yours has PH2.0 or JST, fit XT30: PH2.0 is rated about 2 A and rolling draws 1.8 A continuously, 5 A at stall.
